verses.text: Then all the tribes of Israel came to David at Hebron and said, "Look, we are your own flesh and blood.

In the past, when Saul was our king, you were the one who led Israel out to battle and brought them back. And the LORD said to you, 'You will be the shepherd of my people Israel. You will be their ruler.'"
So all the leaders of Israel came to the king at Hebron. King David made an agreement with them there in front of the LORD, and they anointed David as king over Israel.
David was thirty years old when he became king, and he ruled for forty years.
He ruled over Judah in Hebron for seven years and six months, and he ruled over all Israel and Judah in Jerusalem for thirty-three years.

The king and his men marched to Jerusalem to fight the Jebusites, who lived there. The Jebusites said to David, "You will never get in here. Even the blind and the lame can keep you out." They thought, "David cannot get in here."
But David captured the strong fortress of Zion, which became the City of David.

That day David said, "Whoever attacks the Jebusites must go up through the water tunnel to reach those 'lame and blind' enemies whom David hates." That is why people say, "The blind and the lame cannot come into the house."
David lived in the fortress and called it the City of David. He built up the area around it, from the Millo inward.
David became more and more powerful, because the LORD, the God of Armies, was with him.
Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, with cedar logs, carpenters, and stone workers, and they built a palace for David.
Then David knew that the LORD had made him king over Israel and had made his kingdom great for the sake of his people Israel.
After David moved from Hebron to Jerusalem, he took more slave wives and wives from Jerusalem, and more sons and daughters were born to him.
These are the names of the children born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,
Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia,
Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet.
When the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over Israel, they all went up to search for him. But David heard about it and went down to the fortress.
The Philistines had come and spread out in the Valley of Rephaim.
David asked the LORD, "Should I go and attack the Philistines? Will you give them into my power?" The LORD answered David, "Go, for I will surely give the Philistines into your power."

So David went to Baal Perazim and defeated them there. He said, "The LORD has broken through my enemies in front of me, like a flood of water bursting through." That is why the place was called Baal Perazim.
The Philistines left their idols there, and David and his men carried them away.
Once again the Philistines came up and spread out in the Valley of Rephaim.
When David asked the LORD, he answered, "Do not attack them from the front. Go around behind them and attack them in front of the mulberry trees.
When you hear a sound like marching in the tops of the mulberry trees, move quickly. That will mean the LORD has gone out ahead of you to strike down the Philistine army."
David did as the LORD commanded him, and he struck down the Philistines all the way from Geba to Gezer.
